description: floorboss: every MCP call to a tool floorboss has a recipe for must match the recipe, and a staged draft must match a message floorboss listed. Claude's own file tools never read keys or credentials, never write floorboss's records, and write only floorboss's data folder and the temp folder while a run is under way. While a run is under way, WebFetch opens only the sites floorboss has a reason to, and no web address or search query may be long or span lines. The guard fails closed: if it can't start, crashes or runs past its own 20-second deadline, the call is blocked; a guard that hangs past the 30-second hook timeout is blocked too on Claude Code 2.1.295 or later (onFailure), while older versions let that call through. After an MCP call has run, the guard records what it asked about (a lookup counted, a batch of drafts confirmed), so a no at a prompt stops the rest. The run lock is tied to the session that runs floorboss and ends with it. When the user reports what happened with outreach for a live event, Claude is reminded to record it in floorboss, and on a day the morning brief built itself, told once where it is. What floorboss runs on its own (the morning brief, and the follow-up drafts) is installed, removed and switched on only in the user's own terminal. In any session the guard refuses these names: unattended.mjs with anything but off or status, the job com.floorboss.* or its launchd file, the word launchctl with a word after it that loads or starts a job, and floorboss's unattended folder. It reads them in Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and, in one pass, in the input of a connected (MCP) tool that isn't plainly a read by its name; such a tool's input over 2 MB of values or 512 levels deep is refused, and such tools and Claude's file tools can't write that launchd file, any launchd file that names a scheduled.mjs or unattended.mjs (a different file whose name merely ends in those words is not refused), that folder, today.html or floorboss's other records. It reads text, not the shell: a name built when a command runs, or a copy or link of the script, is not caught, some harmless commands that hold launchctl and one of those words are refused, and nothing that sends relies on it. After a shell command it records two things only, once the command ran after you allowed its prompt: unattended drafts turned on for an event, and follow-ups authorised to go into your drafts on their own. In a run floorboss's own scheduler started (macOS, only if you install it from your terminal), the guard binds the run to its one-time ticket at the session's fresh start, reads the mailbox's and CRM's own answers itself, and returns "allow" for three calls only when every check holds: the mailbox read and the CRM read for a person on the run's ticket, each exactly as its saved recipe with that person's values, and one authorised follow-up draft. Those calls then skip your own prompt rules in that run. Nothing is sent, any call there that would ask is refused instead, and the first refusal stops the run. A call there that fails after it was let through (PostToolUseFailure) is noted and stops the run too. It also refuses, in any session, the follow-up job's install, the launcher's followups mode and the run's token by name.
